newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: FOCUS-CNA Gallo eyes entertainment riches.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-CNA Gallo eyes entertainment riches.

text.p: Leading South African retailer CNA Gallo Ltd enjoyed robust profit growth from its entertainment business and said on Tuesday it was looking at ways to reap more from the sector.

Announcing its annual results, the company said a merchant bank was assessing ways to restructure the group to enable it to capitalise on its entertainment operations, which have overtaken the retail division in contribution to earnings.
The company's retail division reported headline earnings for the year ended March 31 of 27.7 million rand ($6.2 million) -- 28 percent down from 38.4 million rand the previous year.
But the entertainment division swelled earnings by 53 percent to 37.8 million rand from 24.8 million rand -- usurping the retail sector's historic position in the group.
"Retail has always been larger. For the first time, entertainment has moved into first place," CNA Gallo chief executive Dennis Cuzen said.
But issuing a cautionary note to shareholders, he said the merchant bank, which it did not name, was "examining options" on a restructure which would be considered by the board.
"I think it's going to take another six to eight weeks."
While the group increased its turnover by 10 percent to 1,610 million rand, depressed consumer spending due to high interest rates restricted year-end profits, it said.
"Across the board, sales generally were under pressure in the second half. It's really mirroring the customer under pressure and high interest rates," Cuzen said.

Results came in at the bottom end of analysts' expectations. Headline earnings per share were 24.1 cents compared to 25.8 cents previously, while dividends held steady at 10.5 cents. -- Johannesburg newsroom +27 11 482-1003 ($ = 4.474 South African Rand)
